svg.title: Maknae tool credential custody
svg.desc: UML sequence diagram of a tool credential by custody, each step marked live, unreachable or with the issue that builds it: the model's invoke, the kernel's decision before any credential with a deny exit, a token minted in the trust plane and carried in the Permit, a Vault child token or a stored credential fetched by the front end with its own login, the launch helper placing the credential in the container, the output filtered and the credential zeroized before the kernel releases it to the model, and brokered custody where the front end never holds the credential.
svg.text: A tool's credential: who mints it, who stores it, who ever holds it

One tool call's credential, from the model's invoke to the released output. The front end is maknae for a person or maknae-agentd for an agent; the launch helper is the only thing that talks to the container runtime.

The effective credential is what the workspace needs ∩ what the subject holds, decided on every call. A subject only ever uses its own credentials (ADR-0037 decision 6). Each step shows its build state, or the issue that builds it.
«#168» [minted in the trust plane: an agent's task]
«#479» [minted by the front end: a Vault child token]
«#479» [stored in the subject's own Vault tree]
[brokered: the front end never holds it]
shapes, and that a credential is
sees: tool names and shapes, never a credential
4. «unreachable» decide tool.invoke: containment, the tools.yaml ceiling, the role, Tool grants
5. «#168» in a task: the shape's forge needs lie within the task's reach
6. «#479» the workspace's credential bundle ∩ what the subject holds
7. «unreachable» decide the workspace mount and masks; assemble the launch obligation
sees: the task's bindings and reach
sees: the JWT claims; the App key never leaves Transit
timed out: the call ends, no
minted token rides in it, sealed
sees: class names and sealed bytes
16. «#168» open the minted token's seal with the agent's own key
sees: the subject's token and the child
19. «#479» a class cannot be fetched: the call fails, naming it
23. «#481» verify the obligation: kernel-signed, this invocation, used once
27. «#481» remove the credential files; zeroize what it placed
28. «unreachable» filter the buffered output for every delivered value; on a match, withhold it
when the task closes or is held
«live» built, reachable in production · «unreachable» built, no production caller · «decided» in an ADR, not built · «#N» planned in that issue
Every crossing to the model travels in a model turn through maknaed and egress (generated-credential-path.svg); it is drawn direct here.
Slots, not options: the model cannot ask a tool to print its token (#674 PR 3a).
A person cites no task; an agent cites its task. The rest of the decision is generated-tool-invocation.svg.
Authorization before any credential: nothing is minted or read for a call that is not permitted.
A Basic site never writes this policy by hand: Maknae proposes the bundle from a run and grants an agent with one decision.
The whole decision completes before any mint. Pinning the root to the task's own directory is owed (#476).
Agents only: a person's session uses the person's own credential (ADR-0037 decision 6). Minted at the first launch that needs the set (ruled 2026-11-25).
One kind behind a closed interface (ADR-0038 decision 2): a GitLab project token or a Gitea token would be another kind.
The kernel holds a minted set's revocation handle before releasing it. A stored credential or a Vault child token is never in it (ADR-0028). The obligation carries a deadline the helper enforces.
A person's own Vault login or the agent's own AppRole. Vault mints a child only within its parent's policies.
A person: <user_prefix>/<you>/... An agent: <agent_prefix>/<id>/... Never another subject's tree. Stored with maknae credential save (#732).
A child token minted for this call is revoked; a task's minted sets keep their task lifetime.
The helper's separation from the agent is its SELinux domain; on AppArmor same-uid ptrace is restricted by the host only, and macOS is not built (ADR-0035 decision 4).
Read-only root, non-root, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, the runtime's default seccomp. Credential files under /run/maknae-launch/<uid>/, which sensitive.yaml will list (#481).

Built: the value filter withholds an output that matches a delivered value, as raw bytes, hex, percent-encoding, or base64 (standard and URL-safe, at three alignments), and 16-byte fragments of the plaintext. Only EnvVar slots are indexed; line-wrapped base64, xxd-style hex and JSON escapes are not matched (ADR-0026). No tool front end screens output with it yet (#479); the revoke on a match needs #168 PR C. It trusts an intact front end.
DeliveredCredential has no Display or Serialize, so a log line or an error cannot print it; the process writes no core file.
Shorthand: the sealed key travels through maknaed, which carries it unopened; egress takes frames from maknaed only.
Brokering needs the trust plane to end the protocol: SSH here, the model API in egress. A tool's HTTPS through maknae-proxy is TLS end to end, so it cannot be brokered.
